headline: Andrew Baxter sees AI tech market shift from early-cycle semiconductor leadership to mid-cycle broadening across hyperscalers and traditional earners
reasoning: Baxter characterises the recent tech selloff not as a correction or reset but as a 'redeployment', with investors becoming more discerning about where they allocate capital. He argues the market is transitioning from early-cycle to mid-cycle dynamics, where semiconductors led the initial charge but are unlikely to remain pack leaders. Investors are now seeking companies that can demonstrate a genuine return on investment and traditional earnings alongside AI exposure. He draws a parallel to the dot-com era, warning that blindly chasing anything with 'AI' attached carries risk.
quote: I think it's a redeployment, to be perfectly honest. I mean we've seen the semiconductor industry just be charging like a wounded bull. And investors like any time when you see a bull market like that often look for an opportunity to reevaluate their positions... technology is not going to be a smaller part of the future. But I think investors are becoming maybe a little bit more discerning as to where they're putting their money in, not just blindly, because it's got AI mentioned next to it chasing after it, but maybe looking for companies that can demonstrate a return on investment.
